properties.name: CFI Excel for Financial Modeling
properties.description: Comprehensive Excel training focused on financial modeling, covering shortcuts, formulas, and functions essential for investment banking, equity research, FP&A, and corporate finance careers.

properties.name: Excel Keyboard Shortcuts
properties.description: Collection of keyboard shortcuts for PC and Mac to increase productivity in Excel. Essential for financial analysts who need to work without a mouse.

properties.name: Use Keyboard Shortcuts Instead of Mouse
properties.description: To be more productive, faster, and more efficient when building financial models, learn and use keyboard shortcuts. In investment banking, analysts are expected to work without a mouse.
properties.rationale: Reduces time spent on repetitive tasks, increases accuracy, and is a standard expectation in professional finance roles.

reference.chapter: Excel Shortcuts for PC and Mac

properties.name: Mouse-Free Financial Modeling
properties.description: Your mouse will be taken away and you'll be expected to learn financial modeling with only keyboard shortcuts. This is standard practice in investment banking analyst training.
properties.rationale: Speed and efficiency are critical in time-sensitive financial analysis. Mouse usage slows down workflow significantly.

properties.name: Copy
properties.action: Copy selected cells to clipboard

properties.name: Paste
properties.action: Paste clipboard contents

properties.name: Paste Special
properties.action: Open Paste Special dialog for values, formulas, formats, etc.

properties.name: Paste Values
properties.action: Paste only values without formulas or formatting

properties.name: Undo
properties.action: Undo last action

properties.name: Redo
properties.action: Redo last undone action

properties.name: Bold
properties.action: Apply or remove bold formatting

properties.name: Fill Down
properties.action: Fill selected cells with content from topmost cell

properties.name: Fill Right
properties.action: Fill selected cells with content from leftmost cell

properties.name: Go To
properties.action: Open Go To dialog for navigation

properties.name: Find
properties.action: Open Find dialog

properties.name: Find and Replace
properties.action: Open Find and Replace dialog

properties.name: Select Entire Column

properties.name: Select Entire Row

properties.action: Cycle through reference types ($A$1, A$1, $A1, A1) while editing formula

properties.name: Five Time-saving Ways to Insert Data in Excel
properties.description: Five efficient methods to insert data into Excel worksheets: manual entry, copy-paste, import from external sources, data entry forms, and flash fill.

properties.name: INDEX MATCH Lookup Pattern
properties.description: Combines INDEX and MATCH functions as a more flexible alternative to VLOOKUP. INDEX returns a value from a range based on row/column numbers provided by MATCH.

properties.name: IF Combined with AND/OR Pattern
properties.description: Nesting AND or OR functions inside IF to evaluate multiple conditions. AND requires all conditions true, OR requires at least one.

properties.name: OFFSET with SUM or AVERAGE Pattern
properties.description: Using OFFSET to create dynamic ranges that can expand or contract, combined with SUM or AVERAGE for rolling calculations.

properties.name: XNPV and XIRR for Irregular Cash Flows
properties.description: Using XNPV and XIRR instead of NPV and IRR when cash flows occur at irregular intervals. These functions account for actual dates rather than assuming equal periods.

properties.name: SUMIF and COUNTIF for Conditional Aggregation
properties.description: Using SUMIF to sum values meeting criteria and COUNTIF to count cells meeting criteria. Essential for data analysis and reporting.

properties.name: PMT and IPMT for Loan Calculations
properties.description: PMT calculates the periodic payment for a loan based on constant payments and interest rate. IPMT returns the interest portion of a specific payment.

properties.name: DATE
properties.description: Returns the sequential serial number that represents a particular date. Combines separate year, month, and day values into a valid Excel date.
best_practices: Use for constructing dates from separate components
Useful in financial models with fiscal year assumptions

properties.name: EOMONTH
properties.description: Returns the serial number of the last day of the month that is the indicated number of months before or after start_date.
best_practices: Essential for month-end financial reporting
Use with 0 for current month end
Negative months for past dates

properties.name: TODAY
properties.description: Returns the serial number of the current date. Updates automatically when the worksheet recalculates.
best_practices: Use for aging calculations
Combine with other date functions
Be aware it updates on every recalc

properties.name: YEAR
properties.description: Returns the year corresponding to a date as a four-digit integer.
best_practices: Use for grouping data by year
Extract year from date for analysis

properties.name: YEARFRAC
properties.description: Returns the fraction of the year represented by the number of whole days between two dates. Essential for pro-rata calculations.
best_practices: Critical for interest calculations
Choose appropriate day count basis (0=US 30/360, 1=Actual/Actual, etc.)
Used in bond pricing

properties.name: DURATION
properties.description: Returns the Macaulay duration for an assumed par value of $100. Duration measures a bond's price sensitivity to interest rate changes.
best_practices: Use for bond portfolio risk management
Combine with MDURATION for modified duration

properties.name: NPV
properties.description: Calculates the net present value of an investment based on a series of periodic cash flows and a discount rate.
common_errors: NPV assumes cash flows at END of periods
Initial investment should be added separately: =NPV(...) + Initial
Use XNPV for irregular dates
best_practices: Always add initial investment separately
Ensure consistent period timing

properties.name: PMT
properties.description: Calculates the payment for a loan based on constant payments and a constant interest rate.
common_errors: Rate must match period (monthly rate for monthly payments)
Result is negative (outflow) - use ABS if needed
best_practices: Divide annual rate by 12 for monthly
Use type=1 for beginning of period payments

properties.name: PPMT
properties.description: Returns the principal payment for a given period for an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.
best_practices: Use with IPMT to build amortization schedules
Sum of PPMT + IPMT equals PMT

properties.name: XIRR
properties.description: Returns the internal rate of return for a schedule of cash flows that is not necessarily periodic.
common_errors: Dates must be actual dates, not text
Need at least one positive and one negative value
May not converge - use guess parameter
best_practices: Preferred over IRR for real-world analysis
Always use with actual transaction dates

properties.name: XNPV
properties.description: Returns the net present value for a schedule of cash flows that is not necessarily periodic.
common_errors: Rate is annual rate
First date is the valuation date
best_practices: Always use XNPV over NPV for accuracy
Essential for DCF models with actual dates

properties.name: YIELD
properties.description: Returns the yield on a security that pays periodic interest.
best_practices: Use for bond yield calculations
Ensure price is per $100 face value

properties.name: ERROR.TYPE
properties.description: Returns a number corresponding to one of the error values in Excel, or #N/A if no error exists.
best_practices: Use in error handling routines
Combine with IF for custom error messages

properties.name: ISBLANK
properties.description: Returns TRUE if the cell is empty, FALSE otherwise.
best_practices: Use for data validation
Combine with IF for conditional logic based on empty cells

properties.name: AND
properties.description: Returns TRUE if all arguments are TRUE, FALSE if any argument is FALSE.
best_practices: Use inside IF for multiple conditions
All conditions must be true for TRUE result

properties.name: IF
properties.description: Returns one value if a condition is TRUE and another value if it's FALSE.
common_errors: Nested IF can become hard to read - consider IFS or SWITCH
Text values need quotes
best_practices: Keep nesting to minimum
Use IFS for multiple conditions in Excel 2016+

properties.name: IFERROR
properties.description: Returns a value you specify if a formula evaluates to an error; otherwise, returns the result of the formula.
common_errors: Hides all errors - may mask real problems
Consider IFNA for #N/A only
best_practices: Use to handle lookup errors gracefully
Return meaningful defaults like 0 or empty string

properties.name: IFS
properties.description: Checks multiple conditions and returns a value corresponding to the first TRUE condition.
best_practices: Cleaner alternative to nested IF
Include TRUE as last condition for default value

properties.name: OR
properties.description: Returns TRUE if any argument is TRUE, FALSE if all arguments are FALSE.
best_practices: Use inside IF when any condition should trigger action
At least one condition must be true for TRUE result

properties.name: CHOOSE
properties.description: Uses an index number to return a value from a list of values.
best_practices: Use for scenario switching
Index must be between 1 and 254

properties.name: HLOOKUP
properties.description: Searches for a value in the top row of a table and returns a value in the same column from a row you specify.
common_errors: Use FALSE for exact match
Column headers must be in first row
best_practices: Consider INDEX/MATCH for more flexibility
Use for horizontal data layouts

properties.name: INDEX
properties.description: Returns a value or reference from within a table or range based on row and column numbers.
best_practices: Combine with MATCH for flexible lookups
Can return entire row or column with 0

properties.name: MATCH
properties.description: Returns the relative position of an item in an array that matches a specified value.
common_errors: Use 0 for exact match
Returns position, not value
best_practices: Combine with INDEX for powerful lookups
Use -1 or 1 for approximate matches in sorted data

properties.name: OFFSET
properties.description: Returns a reference to a range that is a specified number of rows and columns from a cell or range.
common_errors: Volatile function - recalculates on every change
Can slow down large workbooks
best_practices: Use for dynamic ranges
Consider INDEX as non-volatile alternative

properties.name: VLOOKUP
properties.description: Searches for a value in the first column of a table and returns a value in the same row from a column you specify.
common_errors: Cannot lookup to the left
Column index changes if columns inserted
Use FALSE for exact match
best_practices: Consider INDEX/MATCH for more flexibility
Always use FALSE for exact match in most cases

properties.name: ABS
properties.description: Returns the absolute value of a number (the number without its sign).
best_practices: Use to ensure positive values
Useful for variance calculations

properties.name: SUMIF
properties.description: Adds the cells specified by a given criteria.
best_practices: Use SUMIFS for multiple criteria
Criteria can include wildcards (* and ?)

properties.name: AVERAGE
properties.description: Returns the arithmetic mean of the arguments.
best_practices: Ignores text and empty cells
Use AVERAGEIF for conditional averages

properties.name: CORREL
properties.description: Returns the correlation coefficient between two data sets.
best_practices: Values range from -1 to 1
Use for portfolio analysis and risk assessment

properties.name: COUNT
properties.description: Counts the number of cells that contain numbers.
best_practices: Use COUNTA to count non-empty cells
Use COUNTBLANK to count empty cells

properties.name: COUNTA
properties.description: Counts the number of cells that are not empty.
best_practices: Counts text, numbers, errors, and formulas returning empty string
Use COUNT for numbers only

properties.name: COUNTIF
properties.description: Counts the number of cells that meet a criterion.
best_practices: Use COUNTIFS for multiple criteria
Criteria can include wildcards and comparison operators

properties.name: RANK
properties.description: Returns the rank of a number in a list of numbers.
best_practices: Use order=0 for descending (largest=1)
Use RANK.AVG or RANK.EQ in newer Excel

properties.name: SMALL
properties.description: Returns the k-th smallest value in a data set.
best_practices: Use LARGE for k-th largest
Useful for filtering top/bottom N values

properties.name: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF)
properties.definition: A valuation method that estimates the value of an investment based on its expected future cash flows, discounted back to present value using an appropriate discount rate.
properties.interpretation: Higher DCF indicates more valuable investment. Sensitive to discount rate and cash flow assumptions.

properties.name: Net Present Value
properties.definition: The difference between the present value of cash inflows and the present value of cash outflows over a period of time.
properties.interpretation: NPV > 0 indicates project adds value. Higher NPV is better. Used for capital budgeting decisions.

properties.name: Internal Rate of Return
properties.definition: The discount rate that makes the NPV of all cash flows equal to zero. Represents the expected annual growth rate of an investment.
properties.interpretation: Compare IRR to required rate of return. IRR > required rate suggests acceptable investment.

properties.name: Loan Amortization
properties.definition: The process of paying off a debt over time through regular payments. Each payment covers interest and reduces principal.
properties.interpretation: Early payments are mostly interest; later payments are mostly principal.

properties.name: NPV Function Timing Error
properties.description: Excel's NPV function assumes cash flows occur at the END of each period, not the beginning. The initial investment (time 0) should NOT be included in the NPV function.
properties.cause: Including time-0 cash flow inside NPV() function
properties.prevention: Always add initial investment separately outside the NPV function

properties.name: Interest Rate and Period Mismatch
properties.description: Using annual interest rate with monthly periods in PMT, IPMT, or PPMT functions produces incorrect results.
properties.cause: Not converting annual rate to periodic rate (e.g., monthly)
properties.solution: Divide annual rate by number of periods per year: =PMT(annual_rate/12, nper, pv)
properties.prevention: Always ensure rate and nper use same time unit

properties.name: VLOOKUP Cannot Look Left
properties.description: VLOOKUP can only return values from columns to the RIGHT of the lookup column. It cannot retrieve data from columns to the left.
properties.solution: Use INDEX/MATCH combination instead: =INDEX(return_column, MATCH(lookup_value, lookup_column, 0))
properties.prevention: Consider INDEX/MATCH as default lookup pattern for flexibility

properties.name: Hardcoded Values in Formulas
properties.description: Embedding numeric constants directly in formulas makes models hard to audit, update, and maintain.
properties.cause: Typing numbers directly into formulas instead of referencing input cells
properties.solution: Create dedicated input cells for all assumptions and reference them in formulas
properties.prevention: Establish input section at top of model, color-code input cells

properties.name: Unintentional Circular Reference
properties.description: A formula that directly or indirectly refers to its own cell, creating an infinite calculation loop.
properties.cause: Formula references a cell that depends on the formula's result
properties.solution: Trace precedents/dependents to find the loop. Restructure formulas to break the cycle.
properties.prevention: Plan model structure before building. Use iterative calculation only when intentional (e.g., interest on average balance).

properties.name: DCF Valuation Model
properties.description: A financial model that values a company or asset by projecting future free cash flows and discounting them to present value using WACC or required return.
properties.purpose: Determine intrinsic value for investment decisions, M&A pricing, or strategic planning

properties.name: Revenue Build
properties.description: Section of financial model that projects future revenues based on volume, pricing, and growth assumptions.

properties.name: Amortization Schedule
properties.description: Table showing the breakdown of each loan payment into principal and interest components over the life of the loan.

properties.name: Curso Práctico Excel 2019-365
properties.description: Curso completo paso a paso desde cero hasta nivel avanzado. Enfoque didáctico en español con ejercicios prácticos.
properties.source_book: Excel 2019-365: Curso Práctico Paso a Paso

properties.name: Microsoft Excel 365 Bible
properties.description: Comprehensive Excel reference covering all features from basics to advanced programming. The definitive Excel resource with 1074 pages.

properties.name: AutoFill for Series
properties.description: Using the fill handle to automatically extend a series of values, dates, or custom lists. Excel recognizes patterns and continues them.
steps: Point to fill handle (small square at bottom-right)

reference.chapter: Chapter 2: Entering and Editing Worksheet Data

properties.name: AutoComplete for Data Entry
properties.description: Excel automatically suggests completions based on existing entries in the same column. Press Enter to accept or keep typing to ignore.
steps: Press Delete to clear and type different value

properties.name: Data Entry Form
properties.description: Built-in form for entering data into a list or table. Shows one record at a time with field labels from headers.
steps: Select any cell in data range
Add Form command to Quick Access Toolbar

properties.name: Flash Fill
properties.description: Excel learns patterns from examples you type and automatically fills remaining cells. Works for text manipulation, formatting, and extraction.
steps: Type example of desired result in adjacent column
Press Ctrl+E or Data > Flash Fill

properties.name: Custom Number Formats
properties.description: Create custom display formats using format codes. Doesn't change the underlying value, only how it appears.

properties.name: Freeze Panes
properties.description: Keep row and column headers visible while scrolling through large datasets.
steps: Click cell below rows and right of columns to freeze
Or use Freeze Top Row / Freeze First Column

properties.name: Named Ranges with Name Manager
properties.description: Assign meaningful names to cells or ranges for easier formula creation and maintenance.

properties.name: Data Validation
properties.description: Restrict what users can enter in cells. Create dropdown lists, number ranges, date limits, and custom validation rules.
steps: Optional: Input message and error alert

properties.name: Conditional Formatting
properties.description: Apply formatting (colors, icons, data bars) based on cell values or formulas. Makes patterns and outliers visible at a glance.

properties.name: PivotTable Analysis
properties.description: Summarize, analyze, and explore large datasets interactively. Drag fields to rows, columns, values, and filters.

properties.name: Power Query (Get & Transform)
properties.description: Import, clean, and transform data from multiple sources. Create repeatable data preparation steps.

properties.name: Formato Condicional Semáforo
properties.description: Usar iconos de semáforo (verde/amarillo/rojo) para indicar estado de KPIs o métricas. Visualización intuitiva del desempeño.

properties.name: Tablas de Excel (Ctrl+T)
properties.description: Convertir rango en tabla estructurada. Obtiene nombres de columna, filtros automáticos, formato alternado, y referencias estructuradas.

properties.name: Use Structured References in Tables
properties.description: When working with Excel Tables, use structured references like [@Column] instead of cell addresses. Formulas become self-documenting.
properties.rationale: Structured references are readable, maintain meaning when rows/columns move, and auto-expand with table.

properties.name: Separate Inputs from Calculations
properties.description: Create a dedicated section for all input assumptions, separate from calculation cells. Use different background colors to distinguish.
properties.rationale: Makes models easier to audit, update, and understand. Changes to assumptions are centralized.
properties.anti_pattern: Hardcoding values directly in formulas throughout the workbook

properties.name: Document Complex Formulas
properties.description: Add comments or adjacent cells explaining complex formulas. Use named ranges to make formulas self-documenting.
properties.rationale: Future users (including yourself) need to understand formula logic. Documentation reduces maintenance time.

properties.name: Implement Error Handling
properties.description: Wrap formulas that might produce errors in IFERROR or IFNA. Provide meaningful defaults or messages.
properties.rationale: Prevents #VALUE!, #N/A, #DIV/0! from cascading through workbook. Makes models robust to missing data.
properties.anti_pattern: Leaving error values visible in reports

properties.name: Convert Data Ranges to Tables
properties.description: Use Ctrl+T to convert data ranges to proper Excel Tables. Enables auto-expansion, structured references, and better PivotTable integration.
properties.rationale: Tables auto-expand with new data, formulas copy automatically, and structured references are clearer than A1 notation.

properties.name: Overusing Volatile Functions
properties.description: Functions like INDIRECT, OFFSET, NOW, TODAY, RAND recalculate every time anything changes, slowing down large workbooks.
properties.cause: Using INDIRECT for dynamic ranges, multiple OFFSET calls, or unnecessary NOW/TODAY
properties.solution: Replace INDIRECT with INDEX, OFFSET with INDEX+MATCH, limit volatile functions
properties.prevention: Prefer non-volatile alternatives: INDEX instead of OFFSET, table references instead of INDIRECT

properties.name: Merging Cells in Data Ranges
properties.description: Merged cells break sorting, filtering, PivotTables, and many formulas. Avoid in data areas.
properties.cause: Using Merge & Center for visual formatting in data tables
properties.solution: Use Center Across Selection instead, or format headers separately from data
properties.prevention: Never merge cells in data ranges. Use for titles only, outside data areas.

properties.name: Using Legacy Array Formulas (Ctrl+Shift+Enter)
properties.description: In Excel 365/2021, many array formulas work without CSE. Using CSE unnecessarily can cause confusion.
properties.cause: Old habits from earlier Excel versions
properties.solution: In Excel 365, just press Enter. Dynamic arrays spill automatically.
properties.prevention: Learn dynamic array syntax: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE

properties.name: Wrong Reference Type When Copying
properties.description: Using relative references when absolute are needed, or vice versa. Formulas break when copied.
properties.cause: Not considering how formula will be copied, not using F4 to toggle
properties.solution: Use F4 while editing to cycle through reference types: A1 → $A$1 → A$1 → $A1
properties.prevention: Think about copy direction before creating formula. Lock what shouldn't change.

properties.name: FILTER
properties.description: Returns an array of values that meet criteria. Dynamic array function that spills results.
best_practices: Use with other dynamic array functions
Provide if_empty for no matches
Combine conditions with *
common_errors: Forgetting if_empty causes #CALC! when no matches

properties.name: SORT
properties.description: Sorts the contents of a range or array. Returns a dynamic array.
best_practices: Combine with FILTER for filtered+sorted results
Use -1 for descending

properties.name: UNIQUE
properties.description: Returns a list of unique values from a range or array.
best_practices: Use for dropdown lists
Combine with SORT for sorted unique list

properties.name: SEQUENCE
properties.description: Generates a sequence of numbers. Useful for creating arrays without helper columns.
best_practices: Use with INDEX for array formulas
Generate date series
Create row numbers

properties.name: XLOOKUP
properties.description: Modern replacement for VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP. Can look in any direction, return arrays, and has better error handling.
best_practices: Use instead of VLOOKUP for new work
Built-in if_not_found replaces IFERROR
Can return multiple columns
common_errors: Not available in older Excel versions

properties.name: LET
properties.description: Assigns names to calculation results within a formula. Improves readability and performance by avoiding repeated calculations.
best_practices: Name intermediate results
Avoid repeating complex expressions
Makes formulas self-documenting

properties.name: LAMBDA
properties.description: Creates custom functions without VBA. Define parameters and calculation, then assign to a name.
best_practices: Store in Name Manager for reuse
Document parameters clearly
Use with MAP, REDUCE, SCAN

properties.name: TEXTSPLIT
properties.description: Splits text by column and/or row delimiters. Returns dynamic array.
best_practices: Replace Text to Columns for repeatable splits
Combine with other dynamic arrays

properties.name: TEXTJOIN
properties.description: Joins text from multiple ranges with a delimiter. Can ignore empty cells.
best_practices: Better than CONCATENATE for lists
Use TRUE to skip blanks

properties.name: SWITCH
properties.description: Evaluates an expression against a list of values and returns the result for the first match.
best_practices: Cleaner than nested IF for multiple exact matches
Include default for no match

properties.name: Dynamic Array Formulas Pattern
properties.description: Combining FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, and other dynamic array functions to create powerful data transformations without helper columns.

properties.name: XLOOKUP Returning Multiple Columns
properties.description: Using XLOOKUP to return entire rows or multiple columns at once, replacing multiple VLOOKUP formulas.

properties.name: LET for Complex Calculations
properties.description: Using LET to name intermediate results in complex formulas, improving readability and performance.
properties.example: =LET(revenue, SUM(Sales), costs, SUM(Expenses), margin, revenue-costs, IF(margin>0, margin/revenue, 0))

properties.name: CONCATENATE
properties.description: Joins two or more text strings into one string. Legacy function, consider TEXTJOIN or CONCAT instead.
best_practices: Use TEXTJOIN for delimiter-separated joins
Use & operator as shorthand: A1&B1

properties.name: SUM
properties.description: Adds all numbers in a range of cells. The most fundamental aggregation function in Excel.
best_practices: Use for totaling columns or rows
Handles empty cells gracefully
Prefer over manual addition for maintainability
common_errors: Including text cells returns 0 for those cells, not an error
Circular reference if SUM range includes the SUM cell

properties.name: MAX
properties.description: Returns the largest value in a set of values. Ignores logical values and text.
best_practices: Use MAXA if you need to include logical values
Combine with IF for conditional maximum
common_errors: Returns 0 if range contains only text or is empty

properties.name: MIN
properties.description: Returns the smallest value in a set of values. Ignores logical values and text.
best_practices: Use MINA if you need to include logical values
Useful for finding baseline or floor values
common_errors: Returns 0 if range contains only text or is empty

properties.name: LEFT
properties.description: Returns the specified number of characters from the start of a text string.
best_practices: Use with LEN and FIND for dynamic extraction
Combine with VALUE to convert extracted numbers
common_errors: Returns #VALUE! if num_chars is negative

properties.name: RIGHT
properties.description: Returns the specified number of characters from the end of a text string.
best_practices: Use with LEN for extracting variable-length suffixes
Useful for parsing codes and identifiers
common_errors: Returns #VALUE! if num_chars is negative

properties.name: MID
properties.description: Returns a specific number of characters from a text string, starting at the position you specify.
best_practices: Use with FIND to locate start position dynamically
Essential for parsing structured text data
common_errors: Returns empty string if start_num > string length
Start position is 1-based, not 0-based

properties.name: LEN
properties.description: Returns the number of characters in a text string.
best_practices: Use with SUBSTITUTE to count specific characters
Combine with TRIM first to exclude extra spaces
common_errors: Counts spaces as characters
Returns 0 for empty cells

properties.name: TRIM
properties.description: Removes all spaces from text except for single spaces between words.
best_practices: Always use on imported data before comparisons
Combine with CLEAN to remove non-printable characters
common_errors: Does not remove non-breaking spaces (use SUBSTITUTE for those)

properties.name: UPPER
properties.description: Converts text to uppercase.
best_practices: Use for standardizing data before comparisons
Apply to lookup values for case-insensitive matching

properties.name: LOWER
properties.description: Converts text to lowercase.
best_practices: Use for standardizing data before comparisons
Useful for creating email addresses from names

properties.name: PROPER
properties.description: Capitalizes the first letter of each word in a text string.
best_practices: Use for formatting names consistently
May need manual correction for names like McDonald
common_errors: Capitalizes after every space, including unwanted cases like 'O'Brien' becoming 'O'brien'

properties.name: FIND
properties.description: Finds one text string within another and returns the starting position (case-sensitive).
best_practices: Use SEARCH for case-insensitive matching
Combine with IFERROR to handle not-found cases
common_errors: Returns #VALUE! if text not found
Case-sensitive: 'A' and 'a' are different

properties.name: SEARCH
properties.description: Finds one text string within another and returns the starting position (case-insensitive).
best_practices: Preferred over FIND when case doesn't matter
Supports wildcards (* and ?)
common_errors: Returns #VALUE! if text not found

properties.name: SUBSTITUTE
properties.description: Substitutes new text for old text in a text string.
best_practices: Use to remove specific characters by substituting with empty string
Omit instance_num to replace all occurrences
common_errors: Case-sensitive replacement

properties.name: REPLACE
properties.description: Replaces part of a text string with a different text string, based on position.
best_practices: Use when you know the exact position to replace
Use SUBSTITUTE when you know the text to replace

properties.name: VALUE
properties.description: Converts a text string that represents a number to a number.
best_practices: Use after extracting numbers with LEFT/RIGHT/MID
Multiply by 1 is an alternative method
common_errors: Returns #VALUE! if text cannot be converted to number

properties.name: TEXT
properties.description: Converts a value to text in a specific number format.
best_practices: Use for custom date formatting in concatenations
Essential for creating formatted labels
common_errors: Result is text, not number - cannot be used in calculations directly
Format codes are locale-dependent

properties.name: ROUND
properties.description: Rounds a number to a specified number of digits.
best_practices: Use for financial calculations to avoid floating-point errors
Negative num_digits rounds to left of decimal
common_errors: Different from cell formatting - ROUND changes the actual value

properties.name: ROUNDUP
properties.description: Rounds a number up, away from zero.
best_practices: Use for conservative estimates that should never understate
Useful for ceiling calculations

properties.name: ROUNDDOWN
properties.description: Rounds a number down, toward zero.
best_practices: Use for conservative estimates that should never overstate
Useful for floor calculations

properties.name: CEILING
properties.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance.
best_practices: Use CEILING.MATH for more consistent behavior with negatives
Useful for pricing to nearest 0.05 or 0.99

properties.name: FLOOR
properties.description: Rounds a number down to the nearest multiple of significance.
best_practices: Use FLOOR.MATH for more consistent behavior with negatives
Useful for time rounding to nearest 15 minutes

properties.name: MOD
properties.description: Returns the remainder after division.
best_practices: Use to test if number is even/odd: MOD(n,2)=0
Useful for alternating row formatting
common_errors: Returns #DIV/0! if divisor is 0

properties.name: POWER
properties.description: Returns the result of a number raised to a power.
best_practices: Can also use ^ operator: 2^3 = POWER(2,3)
Use for compound interest calculations

properties.name: SQRT
properties.description: Returns the square root of a number.
best_practices: Use for standard deviation calculations
Equivalent to POWER(n, 0.5)
common_errors: Returns #NUM! for negative numbers

properties.name: SUMIFS
properties.description: Adds cells that meet multiple criteria.
best_practices: More flexible than SUMIF for multiple conditions
Criteria ranges must be same size as sum_range
Use wildcards (* ?) for partial text matching
common_errors: Criteria ranges and sum range must have same dimensions
Text criteria need quotes

properties.name: COUNTIFS
properties.description: Counts cells that meet multiple criteria.
best_practices: More flexible than COUNTIF for multiple conditions
Use for complex filtering counts
common_errors: All criteria ranges must be same size

properties.name: AVERAGEIF
properties.description: Returns the average of cells that meet a single criterion.
best_practices: Use AVERAGEIFS for multiple criteria
Ignores cells that are empty or contain text

properties.name: AVERAGEIFS
properties.description: Returns the average of cells that meet multiple criteria.
best_practices: More flexible than AVERAGEIF for multiple conditions
Criteria ranges must be same size as average_range

properties.name: STDEV.S
properties.description: Estimates standard deviation based on a sample.
best_practices: Use for sample data (most common case)
Use STDEV.P for entire population
common_errors: Ignores text and logical values

properties.name: VAR.S
properties.description: Estimates variance based on a sample.
best_practices: Use for sample data (most common case)
Use VAR.P for entire population

properties.name: MEDIAN
properties.description: Returns the median (middle value) of the given numbers.
best_practices: Use instead of AVERAGE when data has outliers
More robust measure of central tendency

properties.name: MODE.SNGL
properties.description: Returns the most frequently occurring value in a range.
best_practices: Use MODE.MULT for multiple modes
Returns #N/A if no value repeats

properties.name: LARGE
properties.description: Returns the k-th largest value in a data set.
best_practices: LARGE(range,1) equals MAX(range)
Use for top-N analysis
common_errors: Returns #NUM! if k is greater than number of values

properties.name: PERCENTILE.INC
properties.description: Returns the k-th percentile of values in a range (inclusive).
best_practices: k must be between 0 and 1 (e.g., 0.9 for 90th percentile)
Use PERCENTILE.EXC for exclusive calculation

properties.name: MONTH
properties.description: Returns the month of a date as a number from 1 to 12.
best_practices: Use for grouping data by month
Combine with YEAR for year-month grouping

properties.name: DAY
properties.description: Returns the day of a date as a number from 1 to 31.
best_practices: Use for extracting day component from dates
Combine with DATE to reconstruct dates

properties.name: HOUR
properties.description: Returns the hour of a time value as a number from 0 to 23.
best_practices: Use for time-based grouping
Works with both time and datetime values

properties.name: MINUTE
properties.description: Returns the minute of a time value as a number from 0 to 59.
best_practices: Use for detailed time analysis
Combine with HOUR for time grouping

properties.name: NOW
properties.description: Returns the current date and time. Volatile function that updates on every calculation.
best_practices: Use TODAY() if you only need date
Be aware it updates on every recalculation
common_errors: Volatile: causes recalculation of all dependent cells
Timestamp changes - not suitable for fixed recording

properties.name: WEEKDAY
properties.description: Returns the day of the week as a number.
best_practices: return_type=2 gives Monday=1 through Sunday=7
Use for scheduling and work-day calculations

properties.name: NETWORKDAYS
properties.description: Returns the number of working days between two dates, excluding weekends and optionally holidays.
best_practices: Use NETWORKDAYS.INTL for custom weekend definitions
Include holiday list for accurate business day calculations

properties.name: WORKDAY
properties.description: Returns a date that is a specified number of working days before or after a date.
best_practices: Use negative days to go backwards
Use WORKDAY.INTL for custom weekend definitions

properties.name: DATEDIF
properties.description: Calculates the difference between two dates in years, months, or days. Undocumented legacy function.
best_practices: Units: 'Y' (years), 'M' (months), 'D' (days)
Also: 'YM' (months ignoring years), 'YD' (days ignoring years)
common_errors: Returns #NUM! if start_date > end_date
Not in function wizard - must type manually

properties.name: INDIRECT
properties.description: Returns the reference specified by a text string. Volatile function.
best_practices: Use for dynamic sheet references
Combine with ADDRESS for dynamic ranges
common_errors: Volatile: causes unnecessary recalculations
Returns #REF! if reference is invalid
Cannot reference closed workbooks

properties.name: ROW
properties.description: Returns the row number of a reference.
best_practices: Use without argument to get current row
Useful for creating sequential numbering

properties.name: COLUMN
properties.description: Returns the column number of a reference.
best_practices: Use without argument to get current column
Useful in CHOOSE or INDEX formulas

properties.name: ROWS
properties.description: Returns the number of rows in a reference.
best_practices: Use with dynamic arrays to count results
Combine with COLUMNS for range dimensions

properties.name: COLUMNS
properties.description: Returns the number of columns in a reference.
best_practices: Use with dynamic arrays to count results
Combine with ROWS for range dimensions

properties.name: ADDRESS
properties.description: Creates a cell reference as text from row and column numbers.
best_practices: Combine with INDIRECT to create dynamic references
abs_num: 1=absolute, 4=relative

properties.name: TRANSPOSE
properties.description: Returns a vertical range as horizontal, or vice versa.
best_practices: With dynamic arrays, spills automatically
Legacy: required Ctrl+Shift+Enter as array formula

properties.name: NOT
properties.description: Reverses the logic of its argument.
best_practices: Use to invert conditions in IF statements
Useful for negative filtering

properties.name: XOR
properties.description: Returns TRUE if an odd number of arguments are TRUE.
best_practices: Use for either-or-but-not-both logic
Useful in validation scenarios

properties.name: IFNA
properties.description: Returns a value if expression results in #N/A, otherwise returns result of expression.
best_practices: More specific than IFERROR for lookup failures
Use when you only want to catch #N/A errors

properties.name: ISERROR
properties.description: Returns TRUE if value is any error value.
best_practices: Use with IF for custom error handling
Consider IFERROR for simpler syntax

properties.name: ISNA
properties.description: Returns TRUE if value is #N/A error.
best_practices: Use to specifically check for lookup failures
Consider IFNA for simpler syntax

properties.name: ISNUMBER
properties.description: Returns TRUE if value is a number.
best_practices: Use to validate data types
Combine with SEARCH: ISNUMBER(SEARCH(text, cell))

properties.name: ISTEXT
properties.description: Returns TRUE if value is text.
best_practices: Use to validate data types
Useful for data cleaning checks

properties.name: TYPE
properties.description: Returns a number indicating the data type of a value.
best_practices: 1=number, 2=text, 4=logical, 16=error, 64=array
Use for debugging and data validation

properties.name: CELL
properties.description: Returns information about formatting, location, or contents of a cell.
best_practices: info_type: 'address', 'col', 'row', 'filename', 'format'
Useful for extracting file path and sheet name
common_errors: Volatile function - updates on every calculation

properties.name: IRR
properties.description: Returns the internal rate of return for a series of periodic cash flows.
best_practices: Assumes equal time periods
Use XIRR for irregular cash flow dates
common_errors: May not converge - try different guess values
Needs at least one positive and one negative value

properties.name: FV
properties.description: Returns the future value of an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.
best_practices: Match rate period with payment period
Use for savings projections and loan balances

properties.name: PV
properties.description: Returns the present value of an investment.
best_practices: Foundational for DCF analysis
Match rate period with payment period

properties.name: RATE
properties.description: Returns the interest rate per period of an annuity.
best_practices: Use to solve for implied interest rate
May need guess for convergence
common_errors: Returns rate per period - multiply by periods per year for annual rate

properties.name: NPER
properties.description: Returns the number of periods for an investment.
best_practices: Use to calculate loan payoff time
Result is in same time unit as rate

properties.name: IPMT
properties.description: Returns the interest payment for a given period.
best_practices: Use with PPMT for amortization schedules
Sum of IPMT + PPMT equals PMT

properties.name: SLN
properties.description: Returns the straight-line depreciation of an asset for one period.
best_practices: Simplest depreciation method
Returns same amount each period

properties.name: DB
properties.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset using the fixed-declining balance method.
best_practices: Use for accelerated depreciation
More depreciation in early years
